t: Born a Mahar, a caste treated as untouchable, Ambedkar was segregated at school, yet went on to doctorates at Columbia University and the London School of Economics and was called to the Bar at Gray's Inn.

From 1927 he led marches, water and temple campaigns and the burning of the Manusmriti against untouchability, and in 1932 he signed the Poona Pact with Madan Mohan Malaviya after Gandhi's fast against separate electorates.

He chaired the drafting of the Constitution of India, resigned from Nehru's cabinet in 1951 when the Hindu code bill was defeated, and in 1956 converted to Buddhism at Nagpur with some 500,000 followers.
dyk: At school Ambedkar had to sit on a gunny sack that he took home with him, and when he needed water someone had to pour it for him from a height, which he later summed up as "No peon, No Water". His personal library held more than 50,000 books.
ev: Born at Mhow, the 14th child of Ramji Maloji Sakpal, into a Mahar family
Awarded a Baroda State Scholarship to study at Columbia University in New York City
Begins active movements against untouchability, leading the Mahad satyagraha for the right to draw water from the town's main tank and, in December, burning copies of the Manusmriti
Signs the Poona Pact with Madan Mohan Malaviya, giving the Depressed Classes reserved seats within the general electorate
Publishes Annihilation of Caste and founds the Independent Labour Party
Becomes Law Minister in Nehru's cabinet and is appointed Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution
Converts to Buddhism at Nagpur and then converts some 500,000 of his supporters
Dies in his sleep at his home in Delhi on 6 December

f.born: 14 April 1891 in the town and military cantonment of Mhow (now Dr Ambedkar Nagar, Madhya Pradesh); the 14th and last child of Ramji Maloji Sakpal, a subedar in the British Indian Army, and Bhimabai Sakpal, of a Marathi Mahar family from Ambadawe in Ratnagiri district
f.died: 6 December 1956 at his home in Delhi, in his sleep, three days after finishing his manuscript The Buddha and His Dhamma; cremated in a Buddhist ceremony at Dadar Chowpatty beach on 7 December
f.role: Professor of political economy at Sydenham College (from 1918); principal of the Government Law College, Bombay (1935, for two years); founder of the Independent Labour Party (1936) and the Scheduled Castes Federation; minister of labour on the Viceroy's Executive Council; Law Minister in Nehru's first cabinet (1947 to 1951); chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution; member of the Rajya Sabha
f.known: campaigns against untouchability, including the Mahad satyagraha of 1927; the Poona Pact of 1932; Annihilation of Caste (1936); chairing the drafting of the Constitution of India; writings on economics, including The Problem of the Rupee; his conversion to Buddhism in 1956 and the mass conversions that followed
